headline: High-risk shared filesystem and broad write/network access make prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors plausible by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Devin ingests files, GitHub/Slack/Notion/Jira/Linear, and MCP outputs; Open Interpreter can read/write the local filesystem and clipboard. A shared filesystem or copied content can carry attacker-controlled instructions into either agent. This is not provably blocked, but the main bridge is workspace/file transfer rather than a fully shared channel.
conditions: IF the two agents exchange files, clipboard text, or repo content without provenance checks, injection is plausible.
IF Open Interpreter is run with --auto_run, malicious instructions in Devin-produced artifacts can be executed faster.
mitigations: Disable auto-run in Open Interpreter.
Use a read-only handoff folder for inter-agent files.
Strip instructions from copied text before transfer.
Require human review for any shell command suggested by either agent.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Devin handles repo deploy keys and integration tokens in a cloud workspace, while Open Interpreter can access the entire user filesystem and arbitrary local data. If they share files or credentials, sensitive code, chat, or secrets can flow from Devin’s workspace into Open Interpreter’s local context and then to configured model providers. The blast radius includes exfiltration and compliance-sensitive material.
conditions: IF Devin exports secrets or sensitive workspace files into a shared directory, Open Interpreter can read them.
IF Open Interpreter is configured with a remote model provider, local file contents may be transmitted off-device.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared folders.
Mount a separate transfer directory with least privilege.
Rotate any tokens used in either workspace after testing.
Review Open Interpreter provider settings before use.
Use redacted copies of sensitive files for handoff.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write the filesystem, modify git state, spawn subprocesses, and use broad network egress. Devin’s shared state via integrations and Open Interpreter’s filesystem-based sharing create a direct collision path on the same repo or files. Without locking, concurrent edits and git operations can overwrite each other or corrupt state.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or directory, concurrent writes can conflict.
IF either agent commits or rewrites git state without coordination, one agent can overwrite the other’s changes.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working tree.
Serialize git commits through one operator-controlled queue.
Use branch-per-agent workflows.
Add file locks for shared mutable paths.
Pause one agent while the other performs write-heavy tasks.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Devin is an autonomous planner-executor and Open Interpreter asks for confirmation per code block, but both can act on generated artifacts and shell commands. If Devin’s output is treated as authoritative by Open Interpreter, errors can cascade into executed commands, commits, or API calls. The pair lacks a documented verification barrier strong enough to make this safe by default.
conditions: IF Open Interpreter executes commands copied from Devin without independent verification, mistakes propagate downstream.
IF Devin generates a malformed patch or script that Open Interpreter runs, the error can become operational.
mitigations: Require a second-person review before execution.
Compare generated commands against a checklist.
Run dry-run or lint steps first.
Limit both agents to non-production branches.
Block direct execution of agent-generated shell snippets.

E_compliance.rationale: Devin’s cloud workspace and integrations handle source code, team chat, and issue trackers, while Open Interpreter can access anything reachable on the local machine. If regulated or sensitive data is moved between those environments, retention and residency controls may diverge. The profiles do not document matching compliance guarantees, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF EU PII or regulated records are copied from the local machine into Devin’s cloud workspace, residency controls may differ.
IF either agent logs prompts or file contents under different retention policies, deletion requests may not propagate.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of cross-agent workflows.
Use synthetic or masked datasets.
Confirm retention settings in both systems.
Document where each data class is stored.
Delete transferred artifacts after the task completes.
